patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Ecwid and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Ecwid and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Ecwid only if your buying job matches “Embeddable storefront you add to an existing site — Starter $5/mo, Venture $29 annual, Bus” rather than Medusa's shape. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than Ecwid's shape. Workflow advantage: Ecwid leans checkout-conversion; Medusa leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Ecwid and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Ecwid is Embeddable storefront you add to an existing site — Starter $5/mo, Venture $29 annual, Business $49, Unlimited $119 (post 2 Mar 2026 tiles);; Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax..
- Company-size focus: Ecwid (solo, micro, small-business) vs Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Ecwid-leaning checkout-conversion vs Medusa-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Ecwid — Catalog, B2B, and checkout depth trail Shopify-class commerce OS products; Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX.

Limitations — Ecwid: Catalog, B2B, and checkout depth trail Shopify-class commerce OS products; POS / omnichannel is limited versus Lightspeed Retail or Square; Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce).

Poor-fit cases: Ecwid is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Catalog, B2B, and checkout depth trail Shopify-class commerce OS products · Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Avoid Ecwid if you actually need Medusa's motion (Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
